headings: Human Capital Management and Corporate Culture
paragraphs: Ladder Capital is an investment grade-rated, internally-managed real estate investment trust ("REIT") that is a leader in commercial real estate finance. We originate and invest in a diverse portfolio of commercial real estate and real estate-related assets, focusing on senior secured assets. Our investment activities include: (i) our primary business of originating senior first mortgage fixed and floating rate loans collateralized by commercial real estate with flexible loan structures; (ii) owning and operating commercial real estate, including net leased commercial properties; and (iii) investing in investment grade securities secured by first mortgage loans on commercial real estate. We believe that our in-house origination platform, ability to flexibly allocate capital among complementary product lines, credit-centric underwriting approach, access to diversified financing sources, and experienced management team position us well to deliver attractive returns on equity to our shareholders through economic and credit cycles.

Our businesses, including balance sheet lending, conduit lending, securities investments, and real estate investments, provide for a stable base of net interest and rental income. We have originated $31.3 billion of commercial real estate loans from our inception in October 2008 through December 31, 2025. During this timeframe, we also acquired $16.0 billion of predominantly investment grade-rated securities secured by first mortgage loans on commercial real estate and $2.2 billion of selected net leased and other real estate assets.

As part of our commercial mortgage lending operations, we originate conduit loans, which are first mortgage loans on stabilized, income producing commercial real estate properties that we intend to make available for sale in commercial mortgage-backed securities ("CMBS") securitizations. From our inception in October 2008 through December 31, 2025, we originated $17.0 billion of conduit loans, of which $16.9 billion were sold into 75 CMBS securitizations, making us, by volume, one of the largest non-bank contributors of loans to CMBS securitizations in the United States in such period. Our sales of loans into securitizations are generally accounted for as true sales, not financings, and we generally retain no ongoing interest in loans which we securitize unless we are required to do so as issuer pursuant to the risk retention requirements of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act of 2010, as amended, (the "Dodd-Frank Act"). The securitization of conduit loans enables us to reinvest our equity capital into new loan originations or allocate it to other investments.

We maintain a diversified and flexible financing strategy supporting our investment strategy and overall business operations, including the use of senior unsecured notes, non-recourse, non-mark-to-market Collateralized Loan Obligations ("CLO") debt issuances and committed term financing from leading financial institutions. Refer to "Our Financing Strategies" and "Liquidity and Capital Resources" for further information.

Ladder was founded in October 2008 and we completed our initial public offering in February 2014. We are led by a disciplined and highly aligned management team. As of December 31, 2025, our management team and directors held interests in our Company comprising over 11% of our total equity. On average, our management team members have over 29 years of experience in the industry. Our management team includes Brian Harris, Chief Executive Officer; Pamela McCormack, President; Paul J. Miceli, Chief Financial Officer; Robert Perelman, Head of Asset Management; and Kelly Porcella, Chief Administrative Officer & General Counsel. Anthony V. Esposito, Chief Accounting Officer, and Stephanie Lin, Assistant Secretary, are additional officers of Ladder.

We invest primarily in loans, securities and other interests in U.S. commercial real estate, with a focus on senior secured assets. Our complementary business segments are designed to provide us with the flexibility to opportunistically allocate capital in order to generate attractive risk-adjusted returns under varying market conditions. There are a number of factors that influence our operating results. Some of these factors include: (1) our competition; (2) market and economic conditions, including inflation; (3) loan origination and repayment volume; (4) profitability of securitizations; (5) avoidance of credit losses; (6) availability of debt and equity funding and the costs of that funding; (7) the net interest margin on our investments; (8) effectiveness of our hedging and other risk management practices; (9) real estate transaction volumes; (10) occupancy rates; and (11) expense management. Refer to Part II, Item 7 "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" under the heading "Results of Operations."

Balance Sheet First Mortgage Loans. We originate and invest in balance sheet first mortgage loans secured by commercial real estate properties that are typically undergoing transition, including lease-up, sell-out, and renovation or repositioning. These mortgage loans are structured to fit the needs and business plans of the property owners, and generally have Term SOFR-based floating rates and terms (including extension options) ranging from one to five years. Our loans are directly originated by an internal team that has longstanding and strong relationships with borrowers and mortgage brokers throughout the United States. We follow a rigorous investment process, which begins with an initial due diligence review; continues through a comprehensive legal and underwriting process incorporating multiple internal and external checks and balances; and culminates in approval or disapproval of each prospective investment by our Investment Committee. Balance sheet first mortgage loans in excess of $50.0 million also require the approval of our board of directors' Risk and Underwriting Committee.

We generally seek to hold our balance sheet first mortgage loans for investment although we also maintain the flexibility to contribute such loans into a CLO or similar structure, sell participation interests or "b-notes" in our mortgage loans or sell such mortgage loans as whole loans. Our balance sheet first mortgage loans may be refinanced by us into a new conduit first mortgage loan upon property stabilization. As of December 31, 2025, we held a portfolio of 73 balance sheet first mortgage loans with an aggregate book value of $2.2 billion. Based on the loan balances and the "as-is" third-party Financial Institutions
Reform, Recovery and Enforcement Act of 1989 ("FIRREA") appraised values at origination, the weighted average loan-to-value ratio of this portfolio was 68.8% at December 31, 2025.

Other Commercial Real Estate-Related Loans. We selectively invest in note purchase financings, subordinated debt, mezzanine debt and other structured finance products related to commercial real estate that are generally held for investment. As of December 31, 2025, we held a portfolio of 2 mezzanine loans with an aggregate book value of $7.3 million. Based on the loan balance and the "as-is" third-party FIRREA appraised values at origination, the weighted average loan-to-value ratio of the portfolio was 69.2% at December 31, 2025.

Conduit First Mortgage Loans. We also originate conduit loans, which are first mortgage loans that are secured by cash-flowing commercial real estate and are available for sale to securitizations. These first mortgage loans are typically structured with fixed interest rates and generally have five- to ten-year terms. Conduit first mortgage loans are originated, underwritten, approved and funded using the same comprehensive legal and underwriting approach, process and personnel used to originate our balance sheet first mortgage loans. Conduit first mortgage loans in excess of $50.0 million also require approval of our board of directors' Risk and Underwriting Committee. We held one conduit loan with an aggregate carrying value of $28.0 million at December 31, 2025.

Although our primary intent is to sell our conduit first mortgage loans to CMBS trusts, we generally seek to maintain the flexibility to keep them on our balance sheet, sell participation interests or "B-notes" in such loans or sell the loans as whole loans. The Company holds these conduit loans in its taxable REIT subsidiary ("TRS") upon origination. As of December 31, 2025, we held one conduit first mortgage loan that was available for contribution into securitizations. Based on the loan balance and the "as-is" third-party FIRREA appraised values at origination, loan-to-value ratio of the loan was 58.9% at December 31, 2025.

paragraphs: The following risk factors and other information included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K should be carefully considered. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones we face. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial also may adversely impact our business. If any of the following risks occur, our business, financial condition, operating results, cash flows and liquidity could be materially adversely affected. The market price of our Class A common stock could decline if one or more of these risks or uncertainties actually occur, causing you to lose all or part of your investment in our Class A common stock. Certain statements in "Risk Factors" are forward-looking statements. See "Cautionary Statement Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" included elsewhere in this Annual Report.
Our business is subject to change, risks, and uncertainties, as described herein. The risks factors that the Company considers material include, but are not limited to, the following:
•Our success depends upon hiring and retaining qualified personnel and maintaining strategic business alliances.
•The allocation of capital among our business segments varies, which may adversely affect our financial performance.

•We operate using financial models and according to proprietary underwriting criteria in a highly competitive market for lending and other investment opportunities, which may limit our ability to originate or acquire desirable loans and other investments in our target assets and/or our ability to finance and yield a certain return on our investments.
•We cannot predict how government policies, Federal Reserve actions, or changes in the political environment will affect our business and the markets in which we operate.

References to "Ladder," the "Company," and "we," "our" and "us" refer to Ladder Capital Corp, a Delaware corporation incorporated in 2013, and its consolidated subsidiaries.

Ladder Capital Corp is the sole general partner of Ladder Capital Finance Holdings LLLP ("LCFH") and, as a result of the serialization of LCFH on December 31, 2014, became the sole general partner of Series REIT of LCFH. LC TRS I LLC, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Series REIT of LCFH, is the general partner of Series TRS of LCFH. Ladder Capital Corp has a controlling interest in Series REIT of LCFH, and through such controlling interest, also has a controlling interest in Series TRS of LCFH. Ladder Capital Corp's only business is to act as the sole general partner of LCFH and Series REIT of LCFH, and, as a result of the foregoing, Ladder Capital Corp directly and indirectly operates and controls all of the business and affairs of LCFH, and each Series thereof, and consolidates the financial results of LCFH, and each Series thereof, into Ladder Capital Corp's consolidated financial statements.

Ladder Capital is an investment grade-rated, internally-managed real estate investment trust ("REIT") that is a leader in commercial real estate finance. We originate and invest in a diverse portfolio of commercial real estate and real estate-related assets, focusing on senior secured assets. Our investment activities include: (i) our primary business of originating senior first mortgage fixed and floating rate loans collateralized by commercial real estate with flexible loan structures; (ii) owning and operating commercial real estate, including net leased commercial properties; and (iii) investing in investment grade securities secured by first mortgage loans on commercial real estate. We believe that our in-house origination platform, ability to flexibly allocate capital among complementary product lines, credit-centric underwriting approach, access to diversified financing sources, and experienced management team position us well to deliver attractive returns on equity to our shareholders through economic and credit cycles.

In June 2025, we filed a registration statement on Form S-3 with the SEC registering, among other securities, debt securities of LCFH and Ladder Capital Finance Corporation ("Co-Issuer" and, together with LCFH, the "Issuers"), which will be fully and unconditionally guaranteed by us. We own substantially all of our assets and conduct all of our operations through LCFH, and the Co-Issuer is a wholly-owned subsidiary of LCFH. The Issuers are consolidated into our financial statements.

Pursuant to Rule 3-10 of Regulation S-X and Rule 12h-5 of the Exchange Act, subsidiary issuers of obligations guaranteed by their parent company and subsidiary guarantors of securities are not required to provide separate financial statements, provided that the subsidiary obligor is consolidated into such parent company's consolidated financial statements, such related guarantee is "full and unconditional" and, subject to certain exceptions as set forth below, the alternative disclosure required by Rule 13-01 is provided, which includes narrative disclosure and summarized financial information. Accordingly, separate consolidated financial statements of the Issuers have not been presented.

Furthermore, as permitted under Rule 13-01(a)(4) of Regulation S-X, summarized financial information for the Issuers has been excluded because the combined assets, liabilities and results of operations of the Issuers and us are not materially different than the corresponding amounts in our consolidated financial statements incorporated by reference herein, and because management believes such summarized financial information would not be material for investors.

paragraphs: Ladder Capital 是一家獲投資等級評等、 internally-managed 的不動產投資信託（"REIT"），在商業不動產融資領域為領導者。我們發起並投資於多樣化的商業不動產及不動產相關資產組合，專注於高優先順位的抵押資產。我們的投資活動包括：(i) 我們主要業務為發起高優先順位第一抵押固定及浮動利率貸款，以商業不動產為擔保，具有靈活的貸款結構；(ii) 擁有並營運商業不動產，包括淨租賃商業不動產；以及 (iii) 投資於投資等級的證券，這些證券以商業不動產的第一抵押貸款為擔保。我們相信，我們內建的發起平台、在補充產品線間靈活配置資本的能力、以信用為中心的授信方法、多元化的融資來源，以及經驗豐富的管理團隊，使我們在經濟與信用週期中，能為股東提供有吸引力的權益回報。

依我們的商業房貸貸款業務運作，我們發放 conduit loans，這些貸款為穩定、有收入產生的商業不動產財產的首優先抵押貸款，我們意圖使其可供銷售至商業房貸擔保證券（"CMBS"）證券化。自我們2008年10月成立至2025年12月31日，我們發放了17.0十億美元的conduit loans，其中16.9十億美元已銷售至75個CMBS證券化，使我們在該期間按發放金額計算，成為美國最大的非銀行貸款貢獻者之一至CMBS證券化。我們將貸款銷售至證券化，通常會計入為真實銷售，而非融資，我們通常不會保留對已證券化的貸款持續權益，除非根據2010年《多德-弗蘭克壁 Street 改革與消費者保護法案》（"多德-弗蘭克法案"）的風險保留要求，我們作為發行人的義務而必須如此。conduit loans的證券化使我們能夠將我們的權益資本重新投資至新的貸款發放或分配至其他投資。
我們維持一個多元化且靈活的融資策略，支持我們的投資策略及整體業務運作，包括使用高級無擔保票據、非追索權、非市場價值標註的擔保貸款義務（"CLO"）債務發行以及來自領先金融機構的承諾期融資。請參閱 "Our Financing Strategies" 及 "Liquidity and Capital Resources" 以取得更多資訊。

Ladder 於 2008 年 10 月成立，我們於 2014 年 2 月完成首次公開發行。我們由一個嚴謹且高度對齊的管理團隊領導。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們的管理團隊及董事持有本公司權益總額的 11% 以上。平均而言，我們的管理團隊成員在該行業擁有超過 29 年的經驗。我們的管理團隊包括 Brian Harris，首席執行官；Pamela McCormack，總裁；Paul J. Miceli，首席財務官；Robert Perelman，資產管理主管；以及 Kelly Porcella，首席行政官及總法律顧問。Anthony V. Esposito，首席會計官，以及 Stephanie Lin，副祕書長，為 Ladder 的其他高階主管。
我們主要投資於美國商業不動產的貸款、證券及其他權益，專注於高優先順位的抵押資產。我們的補充性業務部門設計為使我們能靈活地根據市場條件，機會性地配置資本，以產生有吸引力的風險調整後回報。以下圖表總結了我們截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日的投資組合（單位為千美元）：
(1) CRE 權益資產金額代表未 depreciated 的資產價值。

影響我們營運結果的因素有許多。其中一些因素包括：(1) 我們的競爭；(2) 市場與總體經濟條件，包括通貨膨脹；(3) 貸款發起與償還的金額；(4) 結構化融資的利潤；(5) 避免信用損失；(6) 債務與權益融資的可得性及融資成本；(7) 我們投資的淨利息邊際；(8) 我們避險及其他風險管理做法的成效；(9) 房地產交易金額；(10) 佔用率；以及 (11) 費用管理。請參閱 Part II, Item 7 "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" 下的 "Results of Operations" 項目。

資產負債表第一順位房貸。我們發行並投資於以商業不動產為抵押的資產負債表第一順位房貸，這些不動產通常處於轉型階段，包括招租、出售及翻修或重新定位。這些房貸結構設計以符合所有權人及商業計畫的需求，通常採用基於SOFR的浮動利率及期限（包括延長選項），範圍為一至五年。我們的貸款由內部團隊直接發行，該團隊與全美範圍內的借款人及房貸經紀人擁有長期且強勁的關係。我們遵循嚴謹的投資流程，該流程從初始的盡職調查審查開始；持續進行全面的法律及貸款審核程序，包含多項內部及外部的檢查與制衡機制；並最終由投資委員會批准或否決每個潛在投資。超過50.0 百萬美元的資產負債表第一順位房貸也需經本公司董事會風險及貸款審核委員會批准。

我們通常尋求將資產負債表第一順位房貸持有以進行投資，雖然我們也維持將這些貸款貢獻至 CLO 或類似結構、出售貸款參與權或「B-notes」在房貸中，或出售這些房貸作為整筆貸款的靈活性。我們的資產負債表第一順位房貸可能在財產穩定後由我們重新貸款為新的 conduit 第一順位房貸。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們持有 73 筆資產負債表第一順位房貸，總帳面價值為 2.2 十億美元。根據貸款餘額及「原狀」第三方 Financial Institutions
1989 年改革、復甦與執行法案（"FIRREA"）評價價值於發放時，此組合於 2025 年 12 月 31 日的加權平均貸款價值比為 68.8%。
其他商業不動產相關貸款。我們選擇性投資於貸款買取融資、次級債務、階層債務及其他與商業不動產相關的結構性金融產品，這些產品通常為投資目的持有。截至2025年12月31日，我們持有2筆階層貸款組成的投資組合，總帳面價值為7.3 百萬美元。根據貸款餘額及貸款發行時的「原狀」第三方FIRREA評估價值，截至2025年12月31日，該投資組合的加權平均貸款價值比為69.2%。

通道首優先抵押貸款。本公司亦發放通道貸款，這些貸款為以現金流商業不動產為擔保的首優先抵押貸款，並可出售給證券化交易。這些首優先抵押貸款通常以固定利率結構，且一般具有五至十年的期限。通道首優先抵押貸款的發放、審核、批准及資金運用，均採用與本公司資產負債表首優先抵押貸款相同的綜合法律及審核方法、程序及人員。超過50.0 百萬美元的通道首優先抵押貸款亦需經本公司董事會風險及審核委員會批准。本公司於2025年12月31日持有單一通道貸款，其總攜帶價值為28.0 百萬美元。

雖然我們的主要意圖是將 conduit 第一順位房貸出售至 CMBS 信託，我們通常尋求維持將其保留在資產負債表、出售這些貸款的參與權或「B-notes」，或出售貸款作為整筆貸款的靈活性。本公司在發行時將這些 conduit 貸款存於其應稅 REIT 子公司（TRS）中。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們持有可供貢獻至證券化的 conduit 第一順位貸款。根據貸款餘額及「原狀」第三方 FIRREA 評估價值於發行時，貸款價值比為 58.9% 於 2025 年 12 月 31 日。

paragraphs: 以下對財務狀況及營運成果的討論與分析應與本年度財務報表及其相關附註一併閱讀。本「管理層對財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析」包含前瞻性陳述。請參閱本年度報告內的「關於前瞻性陳述之警示聲明」及「風險因素」部分，以瞭解與這些陳述相關的不確定性、風險與假設。實際結果可能因多種因素而與前瞻性陳述中所載內容有重大差異，包括但不限於「風險因素」部分所列的風險因素。
提及「Ladder」、「本公司」及「我們」、「我們的」及「我們的」均指Ladder Capital Corp，為一於2013年成立的特拉華州公司，及其合併子公司。

Ladder Capital Corp為Ladder Capital Finance Holdings LLLP（「LCFH」）的唯一普通合夥人，並因LCFH於2014年12月31日進行序列化，成為Series REIT of LCFH的唯一普通合夥人。LC TRS I LLC為Series REIT of LCFH的 wholly-owned subsidiary，為Series TRS of LCFH的普通合夥人。Ladder Capital Corp對Series REIT of LCFH擁有控制權，並透過此控制權，對Series TRS of LCFH亦擁有控制權。Ladder Capital Corp唯一的業務為擔任LCFH及Series REIT of LCFH的唯一普通合夥人，並因上述原因，Ladder Capital Corp直接及間接經營及控制LCFH及其各系列的業務與事務，並將LCFH及其各系列的財務結果合併至Ladder Capital Corp的合併財務報表中。

Ladder Capital為一投資等級評價、內部管理的商業不動產投資信託（「REIT」），為商業不動產融資領域的領導者。我們發起並投資於多樣化的商業不動產及與不動產相關資產，專注於高優先順位的抵押資產。我們的投資活動包括：（i）我們的主要業務為發起高優先順位的第一抵押固定及浮動利率貸款，以商業不動產為擔保，並具有靈活的貸款結構；（ii）擁有並營運商業不動產，包括淨租賃商業不動產；以及（iii）投資於投資等級的證券，以商業不動產的第一抵押貸款為擔保。我們相信，我們的內部發起平台、在補充產品線間靈活配置資本的能力、以信用為中心的貸款評估方法、多元化的融資來源及經驗豐富的管理團隊，使我們在經濟與信用週期中，都能為股東提供有吸引力的權益回報。

於2025年6月，我們向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）提交了Form S-3註冊聲明，註冊包括其他證券在內的LCFH及Ladder Capital Finance Corporation（「共同發行者」及與LCFH合稱「發行者」）的債務證券，這些證券將由我們 fully and unconditionally 保證。我們擁有 substantially all 的資產，並透過LCFH進行所有業務運作，而共同發行者為LCFH的 wholly-owned subsidiary。發行者已被合併至我們的財務報表中。

根據 Regulation S-X 的 Rule 3-10 及 Exchange Act 的 Rule 12h-5，若子公司發行的義務由其母公司保證，且子公司擔保人為證券的擔保人，則無需提供獨立財務報表，前提是子公司義務人已被合併至母公司財務報表中，相關保證為「full and unconditional」，並在下述例外情況下，提供 Rule 13-01 所要求的替代披露，包括敘述性披露及總結財務資訊。因此，發行者的獨立合併財務報表未被呈現。
此外，根據 Regulation S-X 的 Rule 13-01(a)(4)，因發行者與我們的合併資產、負債及營運成果與我們合併財務報表中對應的金額並無重大差異，且管理層認為總結財務資訊對投資者而言並不重要，因此未包含發行者的總結財務資訊。
以下將討論我們2025年12月31日財年與2024年12月31日財年營運成果的比較。有關我們2024年12月31日財年與2023年12月31日財年營運成果的比較，請參閱本公司2024年12月31日財年Form 10-K年度報告的Part II, Item 7「管理層對財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析」。

與本公司作為 REIT 之稅務相關風險
本公司各業務分部間資本配置有所差異，可能對本公司財務表現及流動性造成不利影響。
本公司之成功依賴聘僱及留住合格人員，包括高階管理人員及貸款經辦人員，關鍵人員之流失可能對本公司業務造成重大損害。
本公司可能無法維持戰略性業務合作夥伴關係。
本公司無法預測政府政策、聯邦儲備銀行行動或政治環境變動將如何影響本公司業務及本公司營運之市場。
科技、電子商務及遠端工作已根本改變商業不動產需求模式，這些變動可能對本公司部分債務及股權投資之價值造成不利影響。
本公司獲利可能因利率波動、信用 spreads 變動及相關借款成本而減少。
房貸貸款的預付款率無法確定，預付款可能導致我們資產價值的損失。
通貨膨脹及營運成本增加已對房地產表現及房貸貸款表現造成壓力，並可能持續造成壓力。
擔保措施可能昂貴、耗時，且受州政府、破產、無償還能力及其它債務人與租客救濟法規的限制。
透過拍賣取得的不動產的營運及處分，使我們面臨額外風險，可能損害我們的營運成果。
paragraphs: 下列風險因素及其他資訊包含於本年度報告表 10-K 中，應謹慎考量。下列所描述的風險與不確定性並非我們所面臨的唯一風險。尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前我們尚未知悉或認為不重要，也可能對我們的業務產生重大不利影響。若任何上述風險發生，將可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運成果、現金流與流動性產生重大不利影響。若其中一個或多個風險或不確定性實際發生，本公司 A 級普通股的市場價格可能下跌，導致您損失全部或部分投資於本公司 A 級普通股的金額。"風險因素"中某些陳述為預測性陳述。請參閱本年度報告表中其他地方所附的 "預測性陳述警示聲明"。
本公司業務面臨變動、風險與不確定性，如 herein 所述。本公司認為重要的風險因素包括但不限於以下內容：
•本公司之成功取決於聘僱與留住合格人員，並維持戰略性商業聯盟。
•本公司各業務分部間資本配置有所不同，可能對本公司財務表現產生不利影響。
•本公司在高度競爭的貸款及其他投資機會市場中，依賴財務模型及專屬承銷標準進行營運，可能限制本公司發起或取得目標資產之優質貸款及其他投資之能力，或限制本公司對投資進行融資並取得特定回報之能力。
•本公司無法預測政府政策、聯邦儲備銀行行動或政治環境變動如何影響本公司業務及本公司所從事之市場。
